title: Sharp cocone simplicial sets: vertex isofibration and join associativity
statement:
Use the small simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges and functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations as defined in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], in any fixed sufficiently large universes. For simplicial sets $A,B$, define their sharp join by
$$(A\star B)_n=A_n\amalg B_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}A_a\times B_b,$$
with simplicial operators restricting the ordered block of $A$-vertices followed by the block of $B$-vertices; an empty block is the corresponding pure simplex. In particular $A^{\triangleright}=A\star\Delta^0$.
Let $p:K\to\mathcal C$ be a map from a small simplicial set to a quasicategory. Define the sharp cocone simplicial set $S_p(\mathcal C)$ by
$$S_p(\mathcal C)_n=\{u:K\star\Delta^n\to\mathcal C\mid u|_K=p\},$$
with operators induced by $\operatorname{id}_K\star\Delta(\alpha)$, and its vertex projection $S_p(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ by restriction to $\Delta^n$. Then $S_p(\mathcal C)$ is a quasicategory and the vertex projection is an isofibration: it has the right lifting property against every inner horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i<n$, and for every vertex $u$ of $S_p(\mathcal C)$ with vertex $x$, every equivalence edge $e:x\to y$ of $\mathcal C$ lifts to an equivalence edge of $S_p(\mathcal C)$ with source $u$ and image $e$.
For every small simplicial set $L$, maps $r:L\to S_p(\mathcal C)$ correspond bijectively to maps $t:K\star L\to\mathcal C$ with $t|_K=p$, naturally in $L$. Under this correspondence, the canonical associator of the ordered joins, $(K\star L)\star\Delta^n\cong K\star(L\star\Delta^n)$, gives a simplicial isomorphism
$$S_r(S_p(\mathcal C))\cong S_t(\mathcal C).$$
The correspondence and this isomorphism preserve vertex projections and are natural in functors $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ of quasicategories and in restriction along maps of the indexing simplicial sets $K$ and $L$. No filteredness, nonemptiness or colimit-existence hypothesis is imposed on $K$, $L$ or $\mathcal C$; the cases $K=\varnothing$ (then $S_p(\mathcal C)=\mathcal C$) and $L=\varnothing$ are included.

The sharp/fat comparison (Proposition 4.2.1.5) is not part of this node: it is the existing node lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison. Read online on 2026-10-17; no archived copy in literature/. No matching Stacks tag: these are quasicategorical results, not ordinary categorical statements.

proof.text: Choose a universe of the fixed sufficiently large universes in which both $K$ and $\mathcal C$ are small, and apply the cited statements in it; nothing below depends on the choice. Set $K_0=\varnothing$, $f_0$ the empty map, $q:\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$ the terminal map, and $f=p$. The terminal simplicial set is a quasicategory since every map into it is unique. The terminal map $q$ is an inner fibration in the sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] because an inner horn over the terminal set is simply an inner horn in $\mathcal C$, which fills by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The hypotheses of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration] therefore hold. Its four coslices include $\mathcal C_{p/}=S_p(\mathcal C)$, so this is a quasicategory. Moreover $\mathcal C_{f_0/}=\mathcal C$, while both terminal-base coslices are terminal in each degree. Thus $\mathcal E=\mathcal C$ and its left fibration (lifting $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $0\le i<m$, by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]) $\rho$ is precisely restriction to the last simplex block, the projection $v_p:S_p(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$. Apply [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift] to $v_p$ between these quasicategories: it lifts all inner horns and every equivalence edge with any prescribed source to an equivalence edge. This gives exactly the isofibration clause.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8 (tag 01BZ), specialized to the empty subdiagram and terminal base; compare Proposition 4.3.6.1 (tag 018F). Proposition 4.4.2.11 (tag 019K) and Example 4.4.1.11 (tag 01EW) give reflection of equivalences and the isofibration consequence.

proof.text: Here is the bijection directly from the simplex formulas (it works for any simplicial target). Given $r:L\to S_p(\mathcal C)$, write $u_l:K\star\Delta^b\to\mathcal C$ for the image of $l\in L_b$. Define $t$ on a pure $K$ simplex as $p$, on a pure $l\in L_b$ as $u_l|_{\Delta^b}(\mathrm{id}_{[b]})$, and on a mixed simplex $(k,l)\in K_a\times L_b$ as $u_l(k,\mathrm{id}_{[b]})\in\mathcal C_{a+b+1}$. Conversely, from $t$ extending $p$, assign to $l\in L_n$ the map $u_l:K\star\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ with pure $K$ values $p(k)$, pure $\Delta^n$ values $t(L(\alpha)l)$ for $\alpha:[b]\to[n]$, and mixed values $u_l(k,\alpha)=t(k,L(\alpha)l)$ for $k\in K_a$. Operators restrict each ordered block. If an operator retains both blocks, compatibility follows from $u_{L(\alpha)l}=u_l(\mathrm{id}_K\star\Delta(\alpha))$; if it deletes either block, compatibility follows from the two specified pure-block formulas. Thus both constructions are simplicial, including degeneracies, by the precomposition convention in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Substituting $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ proves one composite is the identity; the displayed compatibility proves the other for every $\alpha$. These are the required inverse bijections, with no colimit or Yoneda theorem invoked.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.5.13, coslice clause; Variant 4.3.5.3 (tag 017Y) and Remark 4.3.3.19 (tag 0172). Agent-written direct ordered-block proof of this correspondence, avoiding an extra colimit-of-simplices dependency.

proof.text: Reassociation of joins is explicit: encode a degree-$m$ simplex in a threefold join by three consecutive blocks of lengths $a+1,b+1,c+1$ summing to $m+1$, with a simplex of the corresponding factor on each nonempty block; permit a length zero block by setting its index to $-1$ and giving it a unique empty label. Both bracketings have exactly this description. The associator keeps the three blocks and their labels, merely changes parentheses, and has inverse the reverse reassociation. Every monotone operator pulls back the same consecutive blocks, so it commutes with the associator even when a block disappears. Now a degree-$n$ simplex of $S_r(S_p(\mathcal C))$ is a map $v:L\star\Delta^n\to S_p(\mathcal C)$ restricting to $r$ on $L$. Step 2 identifies it with a map $w:K\star(L\star\Delta^n)\to\mathcal C$ restricting to $p$ on $K$. Its restriction to $K\star L$ equals $t$ exactly when $v|_L=r$. Precomposing $w$ with the explicit associator yields a degree-$n$ simplex of $S_t(\mathcal C)$ and reversing the operation gives its inverse. Precomposition by $\mathrm{id}_L\star\Delta(\alpha)$ on $v$ becomes precomposition by $\mathrm{id}_{K\star L}\star\Delta(\alpha)$ on the other side, as follows by retaining the same three blocks. These bijections therefore form a simplicial isomorphism. Under the composite vertex projection to $\mathcal C$, both sides restrict $w$ to its final $\Delta^n$ block, so the isomorphism is over $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Remark 4.3.3.32 with Remark 4.3.3.5 (tag 016Q). Agent-written three-block reassociation and application of Step 2 to the iterated coslice; canonical isomorphism, not literal equality of tagged coproducts.

proof.text: For $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$, both directions of Step 2 postcompose each pure or mixed simplex value with $F$, and the reassociation in Step 3 changes no values. Thus their naturality squares commute on every simplex. For $h:K'\to K$ and $g:L'\to L$, the restriction on the join sends a mixed label $(k,l)$ to $(h(k),g(l))$, with the analogous action on pure labels. Substitution in Step 2 gives the restriction of $r$ followed by $S_p(\mathcal C)\to S_{ph}(\mathcal C)$, and in Step 3 the same substitution keeps all three ordered blocks. This proves naturality in both indexing maps. The projection of $r$ to $\mathcal C$ is $t|_L$ by the pure-$L$ formula; the iterated-cocone projection is already checked in Step 3. If $K=\varnothing$, all mixed and pure-$K$ summands disappear, so $\varnothing\star L=L$ and $S_p(\mathcal C)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^n,\mathcal C)=\mathcal C_n$: evaluation at the identity monotone map and pullback of that value along every monotone map are inverse, using the simplex operators in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. If $L=\varnothing$, then $K\star L=K$, $t=p$, and $S_r(S_p(\mathcal C))_n=\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta^n,S_p(\mathcal C))$. Evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_{[n]}$ identifies this with $S_p(\mathcal C)_n$; the inverse sends $z$ to the simplex map $\alpha\mapsto S_p(\mathcal C)(\alpha)z$. These maps commute with every simplicial operator. If $\mathcal C$ is empty and $p$ exists, $K$ is empty; the formulas still give $S_p(\mathcal C)=\varnothing$, a quasicategory with vacuous projection lifts. No step assumes nonemptiness, filteredness, or existence of colimits.
